The Air Dominance and Strike MRB Mechanical Engineering Team supports the production, sustainment, and airworthiness of Group 5 air vehicles and missile platforms. • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent experience

• 5+ years of mechanical engineering experience, including direct experience evaluating nonconformances and dispositioning hardware in a production, depot, or maintenance environment

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security and control commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building continuous assurance, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits.

As Anthropic scales to meet public-company standards, the Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) control environment over our technology stack is one of the most consequential things this team will drive. Within Security GRC's technical controls assurance function, you will be a hands-on senior contributor on what the IT general controls must achieve to support SOX 404 compliance. You will work as a peer to Internal Audit's IT SOX team: Internal Audit tests independently, and you define the control requirements, monitor that controls operate, and make sure evidence is audit-ready before Internal Audit and our external auditors test it.

You will pair with Engineering, Security, IT, and Finance as they design and implement against those requirements, and validate that what ships actually meets the bar. You will also work with GRC engineering to automate evidence collection and continuous monitoring, starting with ITGCs and extending into other areas of security and compliance. This role reports to the Head of Security Controls Assurance and is well suited to someone who wants to stay close to the work and change how a frontier AI company builds its compliance infrastructure.

Key responsibilities

• Define control requirements and acceptance criteria across the core ITGC domains of logical access, change management, operations, and program development for SOX in-scope systems, including home-built platforms where the control has to be designed into the system.

• Set the bar for in-scope systems from day one. As financially significant systems are built, migrated, or replaced, define what the system must provide before go-live, and assess SDLC controls for new system implementations and changes so controls are not retrofitted after the fact.

• Pressure-test changes for SOX impact during design. Review major infrastructure, system, and agent framework changes for control impact while decisions are still cheap, and keep a clear view of which changes alter the SOX scope, key control population, or evidence requirements.

• Perform second-line monitoring and readiness testing. Test key ITGCs and IT automated controls (ITACs) ahead of Internal Audit and the external auditors, including walkthrough preparation and validation that populations are complete and accurate, and support the move from manual to automated control reliance.

• Build continuous monitoring and evidence readiness with GRC engineering. Stand up automated evidence collection and monitoring for ITGCs, map controls to the common controls framework, and materially raise automated evidence coverage while cutting audit prep time.

• Run system and process risk assessments. Identify control gaps in in-scope systems and processes, and recommend remediation that engineering owners can act on.

• Drive control deficiency remediation with cross-functional partners. Track and root-cause ITGC deficiencies surfaced by monitoring, Internal Audit, or external audit; partner with engineering owners on remediation design; and assess whether remediation actually closes the gap before re-testing.

• Support the external audit with Finance and Internal Audit. Prepare walkthroughs, evidence

You’ll own the retrieval workstream end to end, paired with the ingestion engineer, with technical direction from the Solution Architect.

This role carries the most technical risk in the engagement - entitlement filtering is a severity-one commitment. The mission: ship a retrieval API that returns the right passages, with citations, only to callers entitled to see them, at a latency and cost the client accepts, and that the client can version and operate after week 10.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Stand up the Bedrock Knowledge Base and OpenSearch Serverless vector collection in the client’s account from infrastructure code, with the embedding model, chunking strategy, and metadata fields the architect specified.

- Implement hybrid retrieval - vector plus keyword - with metadata filtering by taxonomy, source, status, and review date; tune top-k, score thresholds, and reranking against the golden question suite.

- Build the retrieval API on API Gateway and Lambda per the Integration Blueprint - versioned paths, authentication for the Agent Assist provider, per-client rate limits and usage metrics, structured error responses, and a citation payload with source URL, title, section, and last modified date.

- Enforce entitlement at query time by filtering on permission metadata the ingestion pipeline captures - no restricted passage is ever returned to an unentitled caller.

- Provide the Bedrock retrieve-and-generate reference endpoint used for pilot validation in weeks 7-9.

- Build the quality dashboard - relevance, grounding, and citation scores trended per run; permission test results; freshness lag per source; API latency and error rate; OpenSearch capacity.

- Support the contact center pilot in weeks 7-9 - capture retrieval misses, tune, and re-run the suite before each change ships.

- Write the retrieval and API runbooks including model change, re-embedding, and index rebuild procedures with cost implications.

- Pair with client platform owners in weeks 9-10 and hand over on the transition readiness checklist.

REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

- 4+ years as a software or ML engineer, with at least one RAG or enterprise search system delivered to production and measured with an evaluation suite - not just demos.

- Hands-on with Amazon Bedrock - Knowledge Bases, Retrieve and RetrieveAndGenerate APIs, embedding models - and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector search including hybrid queries and metadata filters.

- Python, with experience shipping Lambda-based APIs behind API Gateway including auth, versioning, and throttling.

- Infrastructure-as-code with Terraform or AWS CDK and CI for deployment into a client-owned account.

- Practical understanding of chunking, embedding model selection, reranking, and the trade-offs between relevance, latency, and cost.

- Experience building operational dashboards in CloudWatch or an equivalent tool.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- AWS Certified Generative AI Developer Professional or AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer Assoc

description:

At IONOS, we don't just manage servers - we shape the digital future for more than 6.2 million customers worldwide with our solutions. As Europe's leading hosting provider and a pioneer in independent cloud solutions, we are building next-generation infrastructure - from sovereign cloud architectures and high-performance GPU clusters to integrated AI automation tools.

What drives us is digital sovereignty for Europe and real impact for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) as well as large enterprises. We work in agile teams, rely on transparent structures, and believe that excellence and innovation only emerge through true team spirit.

Ready for your next step? Become part of IONOS and grow with us.

Our team of highly motivated infrastructure service experts is looking for more teammates. As a Site Reliability Engineer, you will plan, implement, migrate and operate together with other SREs our management services.
Our responsibilities begin with the design of a service and we ensure that our operational requirements will make it to the metal together with the product requirements.

In a culture with an emphasis on creative ideas, agile working methods, initiative, and participation you can expect the following tasks:

Tasks

• Provision, operate and migrate distributed, highly available services on Linux / K8s.

• Improve and develop the full stack from hardware over OS to the application including configuration management and monitoring.

• Development and maintain in-house built K8s operators.

• Support our developers to automate operational tasks and rollouts, provide interfaces for integration for other teams.

• Administration and troubleshooting of our highly available and complex infrastructure including participation in an on-call service rotation.

• Support company goals through efficient operating architecture, active lifecycle management and lean processes in an agile DevOps environment, operate certified, security-relevant infrastructure.

Qualifications

• You have a keen interest in infrastructure topics, good network knowledge.

• Motivation to gain hands on experience with administration of complex services on Linux/K8s.

• Infrastructure as code and automation are important parts our way of working, like us, you are a fan of Open Source, especially Linux.

• Good knowledge in programming or scripting languages like Go and Python or any other programming language.

• The ability to communicate with an international team fluently in English, German is a benefit.

• Degree in Computer Science/Math/Engineering 

• Willingness to undergo extended security vetting (SÜ2).

Benefits

• Hybrid working model.

• Flexible working hours through trust-based working hours.

• At some locations a subsidized canteen and various free drinks.

• Modern office space with very good transport connections.

• Various employee discounts for activities and products.

• Employee events such as summer and winter parties, as well as workshops.

• Numerous training and development opportunities.

• Various health offers, such as sports and health courses.
